items.followUp: Explain the steps involved in testing and debugging a computer program.

rubric.why: Planning sets out an ordered method before the program is written.
rubric.description: Explains that planning decides the steps for solving the problem before coding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the solution is planned as ordered steps before coding.

rubric.why: Identifying the input, processing, and output defines what the solution must do.
rubric.description: Identifies the input, processing, and output.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming all three IPO components.

rubric.why: An algorithm, pseudocode, or flowchart can show the planned solution before programming.
rubric.description: Names a valid way to represent the solution plan.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming an algorithm, pseudocode, or flowchart.

rubric.why: Checking the planned steps can reveal errors before coding.
rubric.description: Mentions checking or testing the plan for errors.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a dry run, desk check, or check with sample data to find errors.

modelAnswer: Planning a solution means deciding the ordered steps for solving a problem before writing the program.
Identify the required input, processing, and output.
Develop an algorithm and represent it using pseudocode or a flowchart.
Check the planned steps with sample data to find errors before coding.

items.followUp: Describe two advantages and one disadvantage of a bus topology.

rubric.why: In a star topology, each device connects to a central device.
rubric.description: Identifies the central hub or switch in a star topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a central hub or switch.

rubric.why: The central device links the devices and handles communication between them.
rubric.description: Explains how devices connect to or communicate through the central device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the connections or data forwarding through the central device.

rubric.why: A device can be added or removed without changing the other links.
rubric.description: Gives the advantage that devices can be added or removed easily.

rubric.why: A fault in one device or link normally does not stop the other devices from working.
rubric.description: Gives the advantage that a single device or link failure does not disrupt the rest of the network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the other devices can continue working if one device or link fails.

modelAnswer: In a star topology, every computer or other device is connected by a separate link to a central hub or switch.
The central device receives data from a sender and forwards it to the intended device.
A device can be added or removed easily without disturbing the rest of the network.
If one device or its link fails, the other devices can continue working.

items.followUp: Explain how encryption helps protect online banking and messaging.

rubric.why: Encryption converts readable information into an encoded form.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption changes readable information into coded information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the conversion from plaintext or readable information to ciphertext or coded information.

rubric.why: A key is used to decrypt the ciphertext and recover the original information.
rubric.description: Mentions using a key to decrypt encrypted information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing decryption using a key to recover the original information.

rubric.why: Encryption helps protect personal and confidential information from unauthorized readers.
rubric.description: States that encryption protects private or confidential information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that encryption helps keep information private or confidential.

rubric.why: Encryption is used to protect information in everyday internet services.
rubric.description: Names an everyday internet use of encryption.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a relevant use such as online banking, online shopping, or secure messaging.

modelAnswer: Encryption changes readable information, called plaintext, into an unreadable coded form called ciphertext.
A key is used to decrypt the ciphertext and recover the original information.
Encryption helps keep personal and confidential data private from people who are not authorized to read it.
It is used in everyday internet services such as online banking, online shopping, and secure messaging.

items.followUp: Give one example each of volatile and non-volatile memory.

rubric.why: Volatile memory needs power to retain its contents.
rubric.description: States that volatile memory loses its contents when the power is switched off.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing this property of volatile memory.

rubric.why: Non-volatile memory retains its contents even without power.
rubric.description: States that non-volatile memory retains its contents when the power is switched off.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing this property of non-volatile memory.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory, such as RAM, loses its contents when the power is switched off.
Non-volatile memory, such as ROM, retains its contents even when the power is switched off.

items.followUp: Draw the truth table for the AND operator.

rubric.why: A two-input truth table must include all four possible input combinations.
rubric.description: Includes all four combinations of the two input values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing the input pairs 00, 01, 10, and 11.

rubric.why: OR is false only when both inputs are false; its outputs for these rows are 0, 1, 1, and 1.
rubric.description: Gives the correct OR output for all four input combinations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing outputs 0, 1, 1, and 1 in the matching row order.
